topics.title: APEC brings major leaders together
topics.summary: Leaders from China, the United States and Russia gathered around the APEC summit in Shenzhen, where trade, technology and international cooperation are high on the agenda.
topics.discussionPrompt: When leaders from very different countries meet, what is one practical thing you would hope they could agree to work on together?

topics.title: Anthropic begins public trading
topics.summary: AI company Anthropic began trading on the U.S. stock market after a record-sized IPO, making its debut a closely watched test of investor confidence in artificial intelligence.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would you ever buy shares in a company whose tools you use, or would that make your everyday app updates feel way too personal?

topics.title: AI demand raises economic questions
topics.summary: The IMF's managing director said booming demand for AI hardware and related technology could add to global price pressures and challenge central banks as they set interest rates.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a new technology makes some things easier but also more expensive, where would you notice that trade-off first in everyday life?

topics.title: Data-centre emissions come into focus
topics.summary: An IEA report highlighted projected growth in data-centre emissions by 2030, renewing questions about how rapidly growing AI infrastructure can be powered more cleanly.
topics.discussionPrompt: If your town got a giant new data centre, what would you care about most: jobs, electricity use, water, or making sure neighbours get a say?

topics.title: Greenland security pact gains approval
topics.summary: Denmark's parliament unanimously approved a security agreement involving Greenland and the United States, updating their defense framework and emphasizing Greenland's role in the partnership.
topics.discussionPrompt: When three places have to share responsibility for something big, what helps most: clear rules, regular check-ins, or a really good group chat?

topics.title: Historic Australian shipwreck is identified
topics.summary: Marine archaeologists announced the discovery of the wreck of the HMCS Spitfire, described as Australia's first locally built warship, 128 years after it sank near Queensland.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you could explore one piece of local history that has been hiding in plain sight, would you pick an old building, a shipwreck, or a forgotten photo archive?

topics.title: Climate science timetable faces concern
topics.summary: A leading climate scientist warned that delays to a major IPCC report could complicate international efforts to coordinate climate action and keep scientific assessments on schedule.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a big shared project slips behind schedule, is it better to protect quality at all costs or publish what is ready and keep improving it?

topics.title: Milder winters reshape bird migration
topics.summary: New research suggests some British birds are staying closer to their breeding grounds as winters become milder, offering another example of wildlife adapting to changing seasonal patterns.
topics.discussionPrompt: What is the first sign of a new season where you live: a bird, a smell in the air, a certain snack, or changing light?

topics.title: Glastonbury unveils younger headliners
topics.summary: Glastonbury announced Sam Fender, Harry Styles and Billie Eilish as headline acts for next year's festival, with Cher set for the traditional legends slot.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you were planning a giant music festival, would you book familiar favorites, brand-new discoveries, or one wild card nobody sees coming?

topics.title: Energy bills forecast to rise in Britain
topics.summary: A forecast pointed to higher household energy bills in Great Britain from January, keeping attention on how families can compare tariffs and manage winter costs.
topics.discussionPrompt: What little home habit makes you feel surprisingly clever about saving energy: blankets, batch cooking, turning things off, or something else?
